title: County of Rosellón
capsule: The County of Roussillon (Catalan: Rosselló) was a Carolingian-era frontier county in the eastern Pyrenees, occupying the coastal plain of the Tech and Têt rivers (modern French département of Pyrénées-Orientales). From around 893 the county became hereditary under Sunyer II, giving it an effectively dynastic character within the broader system of the Spanish March. It was a consistently distinct unit from the adjacent County of Empúries and from Barcelona, with which it periodically fell under shared comital authority. The last hereditary count, Girard II, died childless in 1172, bequeathing the county to Alfonso II of Aragon, who united Roussillon with the Crown of Aragon.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's history is attested in Carolingian capitularies, Catalan cartularies, and Aragonese royal records; territorial extent corresponds closely to the historical plain of Roussillon and is well defined.
